question.problem: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=\sqrt{-6+5y-{y}^{2}}$ and the $y$-axis. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{-6+5y-{y}^{2}} & =0 \\ -6+5y-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ -({y}^{2}-5y+6) & =0 \\ -(y-2)(y-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=2$ and $y=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=2$ to $y=3.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{2}^{3}y\sqrt{-6+5y-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
